text: One day. <break time="0.8s" /> A new group of prisoners arrived. <break time="0.8s" /> And among them was a tall, strong man of sixty. <break time="0.8s" /> With a short gray beard. <break time="0.8s" /> He said he had been arrested. <break time="0.8s" /> Only for taking a horse. <break time="0.8s" /> But added. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had once done something truly wrong. <break time="0.8s" /> And never been caught. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> That he came from Vladimir. <break time="0.8s" /> And that his name was Makar Semyonich. <break time="0.8s" /> And Aksionov. <break time="0.8s" /> Raising his head. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked about the Aksionov family. <break time="0.8s" /> Makar answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That they were rich. <break time="0.8s" /> Though their father was in Siberia. <break time="0.8s" /> And then the others told him. <break time="0.8s" /> How Aksionov had been wrongly punished. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing this. <break time="0.8s" /> Makar slapped his knee and cried. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, this is wonderful. <break time="0.8s" /> But how old you have grown, Grandfather. <break time="0.8s" /> When Aksionov asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether he knew who had killed the merchant. <break time="0.8s" /> Makar said. <break time="0.8s" /> It must have been the man. <break time="0.8s" /> In whose bag the knife was found. <break time="0.8s" /> How could anyone put a knife into your bag. <break time="0.8s" /> While it was under your head. <break time="0.8s" /> It would surely have woken you up. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing these words. <break time="0.8s" /> Aksionov felt sure. <break time="0.8s" /> That this was the man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had killed the merchant. <break time="0.8s" /> And he got up and went away. <break time="0.8s" /> All that night he lay awake. <break time="0.8s" /> Remembering his young wife and children. <break time="0.8s" /> And so great was his anger against Makar. <break time="0.8s" /> That he longed for revenge.
